messages:
oncall-bot: [ALERT] KV cache continuous-batching error-rate spike detected on us-west-2 nodes. 95th latency > 5s, eviction rate jumping 8x. Auto-mitigation triggered: reduced batching window 50%. Paging eng-oncall rotation.

sara nguyen: got the page, looking now. which tenants are hit?

oncall-bot: Top affected tenants: acme-platform (20% traffic), fastfin (12%), and a tail of many small ones. Pattern: sustained prefix KV growth with cache churn after long-tail sequences.

matt choi: I see the same metrics in grafana. batch queue depth is spiking and continuous batching is holding too many in-flight KV handles. Likely config regression from yesterday's batch_v2_throttle change.

rajiv patel: putting link to error dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/boards/kv-continuous-batch?from=now-1h

alexa moreno: @sara can you confirm whether canary for batch_v2_throttle rolled to more than the 5% target? I thought we gated it.

sara nguyen: checking rollout history... yes — it shows 5% global but with per-customer override for acme-platform (they were opted in for perf testing). That explains ACME being hot.

beth (cust-eng): FYI we've already had one support ticket from ACME about slow API responses. I replied we were investigating. If you need to throttle/override for just them let me know and I can coordinate.

matt choi: immediate mitigation options: 1) kill per-customer override for acme to revert them to 5% canary; 2) globally reduce batch window further (impacts latency/cost); 3) enable emergency per-tenant throttle for top N. Prefer 1 + 3.

sara nguyen: i'll take ownership. matt, can you prepare a per-tenant override command and a rollback snippet? i'll page cust-eng.

matt choi: prepared snippets below. use with care.

```
# revoke per-customer canary for acme-platform
redwood-ctl flag set batch_v2_throttle --scope=customer:acme-platform --value=default --reason="live-mitigation: revert acme opt-in"

# emergency throttle for top tenants (reduce batch window to 30ms for specific customers)
redwood-ctl config patch --customer acme-platform --json '{"batch_window_ms":30}' --author=sara
```

rajiv patel: I'll stand by to adjust autoscaler if this creates downstream CPU pressure.

sara nguyen: executing revoke now.

deploy-bot: deploy started: flag-change batch_v2_throttle revert for scope customer:acme-platform (initiated by sara nguyen)

sara nguyen: done — revoke issued. watching metrics.

oncall-bot: flag-change completed. latency for acme-platform 95th now trending down after ~60s. overall eviction rate decreasing.

matt choi: good sign. I'm going to push emergency per-tenant batch_window patch for top-5 tenants to avoid ripples while we assess.

sara nguyen: please do, include the list: acme-platform, fastfin, payly, streamly, metricsco. beth — heads up I'll patch acme via the control plane and follow-up with status.

beth (cust-eng): pulling ACME stakeholders into a short bridge. they want ETA and whether we rolled them back to the default.

alexa moreno: ops-signal: adding a canary gating check to prevent per-customer opt-ins from bypassing global canary policy. I'll open a follow-up ticket but not in this hot path.

matt choi: patch command executed for top-5.

deploy-bot: config-patch succeeded for 5 customers.

oncall-bot: system note — overall 95th latency back to 1.2s from 5s within 3 minutes. eviction rate normalized. Still monitoring for residual KV churn.

sara nguyen: handing off to eng-sre for post-mortem and rollback validation. I'm going offline for incident page. @matt you have run of this thread for remediation follow-ups.

matt choi: taking it. immediate next steps: 1) run the canary audit to ensure no other customers have overrides that bypass canary percentage; 2) add temporary rule to prevent new per-customer opt-ins for batch_v2_throttle until root cause identified; 3) schedule analysis of sequence-length distributions that caused KV growth.

rajiv patel: I'll look at autoscaler delta logs and confirm no CPU/GPU saturation spike from the batch_window patches.

alexa moreno: created ticket INF-8721: "per-customer canary bypass -> audit + guardrails". assigning to eng-runtime and devex.

beth (cust-eng): ACME on the bridge confirmed performance improvement. They asked for a timeline for a permanent fix. I'll keep them updated and suggest guarded re-rolling once we harden guardrails.

sara nguyen: short postmortem notes for handover: root cause: per-customer opt-in allowed bypassing global canary percent; batch_v2_throttle config combined with long-sequence KV patterns amplified cache churn. Mitigation: revoke per-customer opt-in for acme, emergency batch_window reduce for top tenants, and temporary block on new per-customer overrides.

matt choi: leaving a quick remediation artifact: runbook excerpt below.

```
Runbook - Live KV/Batch Regression
1) If alert: identify top 3 tenants by eviction rate.
2) Revoke per-customer flag: `redwood-ctl flag set batch_v2_throttle --scope=customer:<id> --value=default`
3) Apply emergency per-tenant batch_window: `redwood-ctl config patch --customer <id> --json '{"batch_window_ms":30}'`
4) Monitor 95th latency and eviction_rate for 10 minutes.
5) If stable, escalate to postmortem and schedule guardrail rollout.
```

oncall-bot: incident closed: acute surge mitigated and handoff completed. Please file incident report in postmortems with relevant traces and the ACME impact notes.

sara nguyen: thanks team. I'll create the postmortem and link to this thread. leaving a follow-up action item: ensure feature-flagging infra enforces global-canary caps by EOD tomorrow.

matt choi: assigning myself to the post-incident rollout for guardrails. cc: @alexa for devex changes.

beth (cust-eng): ACME is satisfied with the proactive communication. I'll add their feedback to the postmortem.

alexa moreno: quick note — we saw one smaller tenant still showing intermittent tails; raising INF-8730 to track slow-tail mitigation via KV TTL tuning.

matt choi: final: I'll keep the emergency per-tenant patches active for 2 hours and then revert if stable. will update thread when reverted.

oncall-bot: follow-up reminder queued for +2h to check revert status.

matt choi: 2h check — all signals stable, reverting emergency patches now.

deploy-bot: revert config-patch succeeded for 5 customers (initiated by matt choi).

oncall-bot: final status: metrics stable for 30m after revert. incident resolved.

sara nguyen: closing handoff. postmortem link: https://wiki.redwood/incidents/INF-8719-kv-batch-optin-surge

beth (cust-eng): thanks everyone.

matt choi: good work.
